newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called up after stock data, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called up after stock data, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Thursday after a lower-than-expected storage number boosted August on ACCESS and near 100 degree F heat covered Texas and southern plains.
"We are attempting some convergence with cash," one trader said, noting early Henry Hub cash prices were talked firmer at $2.22-2.24.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.16 to $2.17 after settling Wednesday at $2.148 per million British thermal units.
August, which expires Tuesday, last traded on ACCESS 1.3 cents firmer at $2.161.
American Gas Association said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 58 bcf, well below average estimates of 75-80 bcf. Overall stocks were 183 bcf, or 11 percent, above year-ago levels.

Eastern inventories increased by 48 bcf last week and were still 56 bcf, or six percent, over last year. Consuming region West storage, which gained 10 bcf last week, continued to lag 1996 levels by about six percent. Stocks in the producing region were unchanged and still 41 percent above year-ago.
Chart traders said August resistance was at $2.21 and then at $2.29 and $2.36. Support was seen at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8.
In Wednesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed three cents to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were four cents higher around $2.10, while New York city gate gas was up slightly at $2.40.
